'''El Tráfico''', also known as the '''Los Angeles Derby''', is a [[List of association football rivalries|soccer rivalry]] between the two [[Major League Soccer]] (MLS) clubs based in the [[Greater Los Angeles]] area, the [[LA Galaxy]] and [[Los Angeles FC]].<ref name="Wiebe2018">{{cite news |last=Wiebe |first=Andrew |date=March 28, 2018 |title=Wiebe: First-ever "El Trafico" will lay stakes for LA Galaxy-LAFC rivalry |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2018/03/28/wiebe-first-ever-el-trafico-will-lay-stakes-la-galaxy-lafc-rivalry |work=MLSsoccer.com |access-date=March 29, 2018}}</ref><ref name="LATimes-2018Mar">{{cite news |last=Baxter |first=Kevin |date=March 28, 2018 |title=Galaxy and LAFC fans are taking new rivalry very seriously |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/la-sp-galaxy-lafc-20180328-story.html |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=March 29, 2018}}</ref> The rivalry is one of two crosstown derbies in MLS, alongside the [[Hudson River Derby]] in the [[New York City]] area. It replaced the [[SuperClasico]] between the LA Galaxy and defunct [[Chivas USA]].

This rivalry has been characterized by dramatic goals, high scoring, and consistently close results, as well as mutual fan animosity. El Tráfico quickly became one of the most popular and contested rivalries in the league; in addition to regular season play, the Galaxy and LAFC have played each other in the [[MLS Cup playoffs]] and [[U.S. Open Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Ruthven |first=Graham |date=October 20, 2022 |title=Manufactured rivalries don't work: LA's El Tráfico is an exception |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/oct/20/el-trafico-los-angeles-galaxy-lafc-mls-soccer-derby |work=[[The Guardian]] |accessdate=November 24, 2022}}</ref>

==Background==

Los Angeles FC was established in 2014, shortly after the dissolution of [[Chivas USA]], an MLS franchise based in Los Angeles and owned by [[C.D. Guadalajara]]. Chivas shared the [[Dignity Health Sports Park|StubHub Center]] in the city of [[Carson, California]], originally known as the Home Depot Center (2003–2013) and now known as Dignity Health Sports Park, with the Galaxy but had far lower attendances during its final years of operation.<ref name="LATimes-2018Mar30">{{cite news |last=Baxter |first=Kevin |date=March 30, 2018 |title='Proper rivalry' leaves Galaxy defending home turf against LAFC |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/la-sp-lafc-galaxy-20180330-story.html |work=Los Angeles Times |access-date=March 31, 2018}}</ref> The two teams competed in the [[SuperClasico]], named for the [[El Súper Clásico (Mexico)|Mexican rivalry]] between Guadalajara and [[Club América]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Parker |first=Graham |date=May 17, 2012 |title=LA Story Part One: Chivas USA |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2012/may/17/mls-la-story-part-one-chivas-usa |work=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=March 31, 2018}}</ref> The two teams met 31 times in ten seasons, with the Galaxy winning 20 matches and Chivas winning four.<ref name="Wiebe2018"/><ref name="LATimes-2018Mar30"/>

Los Angeles FC built Banc of California Stadium, now known as [[BMO Stadium]], in Exposition Park in [[Los Angeles, California]], approximately {{convert|13|mi|km}} north of [[Carson, California]], on [[Interstate 110 (California)|Interstate 110]].<ref name="LATimes-2018Mar30"/>

==History==
{{See also|March 2018 LA Galaxy–Los Angeles FC game}}
The first match between the two senior teams, LAFC's third-ever regular season game,<ref>{{cite web |last=Butler |first=Dylan |date=March 29, 2018 |title=LA Galaxy vs. LAFC: 2018 MLS Match Preview |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2018/03/29/la-galaxy-vs-lafc-2018-mls-match-preview |website=MLSsoccer.com |access-date=March 31, 2018}}</ref> was played on March 31, 2018, at the [[Dignity Health Sports Park|StubHub Center]]. Despite LAFC leading 3–0 after 60 minutes, the match ended in a 4–3 win for the Galaxy, including two goals from substitute [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]] on his club debut.<ref>{{cite news |last=Baxter |first=Kevin |date=March 31, 2018 |title=Zlatan Ibrahimovic scores two late goals to lift Galaxy to a 4-3 victory over LAFC |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/la-sp-lafc-galaxy-20180331-story.html |work=Los Angeles Times |access-date=March 31, 2018}}</ref> The teams played at [[BMO Stadium|Banc of California Stadium]] on July 26 and was followed by a second match at the StubHub Center on August 24 during MLS Rivalry Week.<ref>{{cite news |last=Baxter |first=Kevin |date=January 4, 2018 |title=LAFC to meet Galaxy three times in first MLS season |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/la-sp-galaxy-lafc-schedules-20180104-story.html |work=Los Angeles Times |access-date=March 31, 2018}}</ref> The second meeting, on July 26, ended in a 2–2 draw at the Banc of California Stadium. Six fans were arrested in clashes between fans at the stadium, where seats were damaged and fights broke out.<ref>{{cite news |last=Baxter |first=Kevin |date=July 27, 2018 |title=LAFC-Galaxy game marred by vandalism and altercations |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/la-sp-lafc-galaxy-vandalism-20180727-story.html |work=Los Angeles Times |access-date=July 28, 2018}}</ref> The final meeting of the two teams in 2018, played a month later on August 24, ended in a 1–1 draw at the StubHub Center.<ref>{{cite news |last=Baxter |first=Kevin |date=August 24, 2018 |title=With playoff positions on the line, Galaxy and LAFC end L.A. Derby with 1-1 draw |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/la-sp-lafc-galaxy-20180824-story.html |work=Los Angeles Times |access-date=July 19, 2020}}</ref>

The first El Tráfico match of the 2019 season, played in July at Dignity Health Sports Park (formerly the StubHub Center), ended in a 3–2 victory for the hosting LA Galaxy. Ibrahimović's scored all three Galaxy goals and earned a [[hat-trick (association football)|hat-trick]], while [[Carlos Vela]] scored both of LAFC's goals.<ref>{{cite news |last=Baxter |first=Kevin |date=July 19, 2019 |title=El Trafico: Zlatan Ibrahimovic's hat trick gets Galaxy the victory in testy match with LAFC |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/story/2019-07-19/lafc-galaxy-gamer |work=Los Angeles Times |access-date=July 19, 2020}}</ref> The visiting LAFC supporters came in a 17-bus convoy and wore camouflage outfits as part of a "united front", having been inspired by a similar display by German club [[Dynamo Dresden]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Dwyer |first=Alex |date=July 22, 2019 |title=LAFC supporters groups don camouflage for "united front" on Trafico trip |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2019/07/22/lafc-supporters-groups-don-camouflage-united-front-trafico-trip |work=MLSsoccer.com |access-date=July 19, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Elliott |first=Helene |date=July 19, 2019 |title=Column: El Trafico continues to deliver the makings of a great rivalry |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/story/2019-07-19/lafc-galaxy-column |work=Los Angeles Times |access-date=July 19, 2020}}</ref> The return fixture at Banc of California Stadium a month later ended in a 3–3 draw, with two goals apiece for Ibrahimović and [[Latif Blessing]] after a second-half comeback from LAFC.<ref>{{cite news |last=Calhoun |first=Damian |date=August 25, 2019 |title=LAFC rallies from two-goal deficit to finish with draw against Galaxy |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/08/25/lafc-rallies-from-two-goal-deficit-to-finish-with-draw-against-galaxy/ |work=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |access-date=July 19, 2020}}</ref>

The two teams met in the Western Conference Semifinals during the [[2019 MLS Cup Playoffs]], which was hosted by top-seeded LAFC after the Galaxy advanced from the first round against [[Minnesota United FC]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Baxter |first=Kevin |date=October 20, 2019 |title=Galaxy beat Minnesota, will face LAFC next in MLS playoffs |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/story/2019-10-20/galaxy-beat-minnesota-will-face-lafc-next-in-mls-playoffs |work=Los Angeles Times |access-date=July 19, 2020}}</ref> LAFC won 5–3, breaking a six-match winless streak against the Galaxy, with pairs of goals scored by Vela and [[Adama Diomande]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Baxter |first=Kevin |date=October 24, 2019 |title=Carlos Vela and Adama Diomande lead LAFC to El Trafico playoff win over Galaxy |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/story/2019-10-24/carlos-vela-adama-diomande-lafc-el-trafico-mls-playoff-win-galaxy |work=Los Angeles Times |access-date=July 19, 2020}}</ref> LAFC advanced to the Conference Final, where they lost 3–1 to [[Seattle Sounders FC]], the eventual [[MLS Cup 2019]] champions.<ref>{{cite news |last=Baxter |first=Kevin |date=October 29, 2019 |title=Magic runs out for LAFC and Carlos Vela in season-ending loss to Seattle Sounders |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/story/2019-10-29/lafc-eliminated-seattle-sounders-mls-playoffs-western-conference-finals |work=Los Angeles Times |access-date=July 19, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Calkins |first=Matt |date=November 10, 2019 |title=For Sounders fans, Sunday's MLS Cup lived up to the hype and may never be topped |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/sounders/for-sounders-fans-sundays-mls-cup-lived-up-to-the-hype-and-may-never-be-topped/ |work=[[The Seattle Times]] |access-date=July 19, 2020}}</ref>

The opening El Tráfico fixture of the 2020 season was scheduled for May 16, but MLS suspended all operations in March due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Carlisle |first=Jeff |date=December 19, 2019 |title=Can't-miss MLS matches in 2020 include El Trafico, debuts of Nashville and Beckham's Inter Miami |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/major-league-soccer/story/4016131/cant-miss-mls-matches-in-2020-include-el-traficodebuts-of-nashville-and-beckhams-inter-miami |publisher=ESPN |access-date=July 19, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Baxter |first=Kevin |date=March 19, 2020 |title=MLS extends suspension of season until May 10 due to COVID-19 pandemic |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/story/2020-03-19/mls-further-suspends-season-may-10-coronavirus |work=Los Angeles Times |access-date=July 19, 2020}}</ref> The two teams were drawn into Group F of the [[MLS is Back Tournament]], which would be played without spectators at the [[ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex]] in Florida.<ref>{{cite news |last=Baxter |first=Kevin |date=June 11, 2020 |title=LAFC and Galaxy will play in same group in MLS season restart tournament |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/story/2020-06-11/lafc-galaxy-will-play-in-same-group-in-mls-season-tournament-coronavirus |work=Los Angeles Times |access-date=July 19, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Baxter |first=Kevin |date=July 17, 2020 |title=Fanless El Tráfico rivalry between LAFC and Galaxy won't feel the same |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/story/2020-07-17/el-trafico-matchup-lafc-galaxy-wont-be-same-mls-fans |work=Los Angeles Times |access-date=July 19, 2020}}</ref> LAFC and the Galaxy met in the second matchday on July 18, 2020, with Vela opting out of the tournament and the Galaxy's [[Javier Hernández]] injured. LAFC won 6–2, setting a new record for largest margin of victory in El Tráfico, with four goals from [[Diego Rossi]]; both of the Galaxy's goals had come in the first 31 minutes, from an own goal and a penalty kick.<ref>{{cite news |last=Baxter |first=Kevin |date=July 18, 2020 |title=Diego Rossi's four goals power LAFC to victory over Galaxy in MLS is Back Tournament |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/story/2020-07-18/diego-rossi-four-goals-power-lafc-to-victory-over-galaxy-in-mls-tournament |work=Los Angeles Times |access-date=July 19, 2020}}</ref> On August 22, 2020, the Galaxy recorded the first El Tráfico away win with a 2–0 win and the first clean sheet at the Banc of California Stadium. On May 25, 2022, the Galaxy defeated LAFC 3–1 at [[Dignity Health Sports Park]] in the first ever [[US Open Cup]] El Tráfico with goals by [[Kévin Cabral]], Javier Hernández, and [[Dejan Joveljic]] for the Galaxy and [[Ryan Hollingshead]] for LAFC. In their second playoff meeting at Banc of California Stadium on October 20, 2022, LAFC won 3–2. 

The Galaxy planned to host their 2023 season opener on February 25 against LAFC at the [[Rose Bowl (stadium)|Rose Bowl]], the Galaxy's former stadium from 1996 to 2002.<ref name="Times-Rose">{{cite news |last=Baxter |first=Kevin |date=September 27, 2022 |title=Galaxy and LAFC to open 2023 season against each other at Rose Bowl |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/story/2022-09-27/galaxy-lafc-open-2023-mls-season-rose-bowl |work=Los Angeles Times |accessdate=September 27, 2022}}</ref> It was postponed to July 4 due to heavy wind and rain in the area brought by a [[February 2023 North American winter storm|major winter storm]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Baxter |first=Kevin |date=February 24, 2023 |title=Galaxy-LAFC game at the Rose Bowl postponed until July 4 |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/story/2023-02-24/galaxy-lafc-game-rose-bowl-postponed-weather-el-trafico |work=Los Angeles Times |accessdate=February 24, 2023}}</ref> The Rose Bowl match had 82,110 spectators, setting a new MLS record for standalone attendance, and was split between the two teams; the Galaxy won 2–1.<ref>{{cite news |last=Baxter |first=Kevin |date=July 4, 2023 |title=Galaxy hold off LAFC in front of record crowd at Rose Bowl |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/story/2023-07-04/lafc-galaxy-july-4-mls-game-recap |work=Los Angeles Times |accessdate=July 4, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Sigal |first=Jonathan |date=July 4, 2023 |title=MLS history! El Tráfico at Rose Bowl sets single-game attendance record |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/mls-history-el-trafico-at-rose-bowl-sets-single-game-attendance-record |work=MLSsoccer.com |accessdate=July 4, 2023}}</ref> A third match against designated rivals was added to the MLS schedule in 2023; LAFC expressed interest in potentially hosting the game at either the [[Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum|Coliseum]] or [[SoFi Stadium]] in 2024.<ref name="Times-Rose"/>

The 2024 match at the Rose Bowl resulted in a $100,000 fine for the Galaxy due to misconduct by their supporters, including the lighting of flares during play.<ref>{{cite news |last=Baxter |first=Kevin |date=July 12, 2024 |title=MLS fines Galaxy $100,000 for 'serious misconduct' by fans at Rose Bowl |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/galaxy/story/2024-07-12/mls-fines-galaxy-100000-fan-misconduct-rose-bowl |work=Los Angeles Times |accessdate=July 19, 2024}}</ref> For 2025, the games will return to the clubs' respective home stadiums due to the balanced schedule.

On December 7, 2024, [[John McCarthy (soccer)|John McCarthy]] became the first person to win the [[MLS Cup]] with both clubs, previously winning with [[Los Angeles FC]] in [[2022 MLS Cup|2022]].

==Fan activities==

In January 2018, a mural commissioned by LAFC in [[Pico-Union, Los Angeles|Pico-Union]] was vandalized with the colors of the LA Galaxy within hours of being completed and unveiled. This followed an earlier incident where paint in LAFC's colors was sprayed over an LA Galaxy mural at [[Hawthorne Memorial Park]] and a Galaxy billboard.<ref name="LATimes-2018Mar"/><ref>{{cite news |last=Nachman |first=Gideon |date=May 29, 2017 |title=Is it possible to manufacture a football rivalry? MLS has tried ... |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2017/may/29/is-it-possible-to-manufacture-a-football-rivalry-mls-has-tried- |work=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=April 16, 2018}}</ref> Both fanbases later defaced property during the inaugural year of the rivalry.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.lagconfidential.com/2017/5/23/15683380/some-angelino-mls-fans-want-a-tagging-war|title=Some Angelinos want a tagging war|work=LAG Confidential|access-date=April 3, 2018}}</ref>

The clubs and fanbases have created a unique animosity between one another. For example, many LAFC fans refuse to use the name "LA Galaxy," instead opting for "Carson Galaxy" due to the fact that the Galaxy do not play in the city of Los Angeles but in Carson, California, a city in the county of Los Angeles. In addition, LAFC itself simply calls its rival "Galaxy" and often mocks their fans as "suburbanites". {{cn|date=October 2022}} LA Galaxy fans frequently mock LAFC and its fans as "Chivas 2.0" as an allusion to the former Chivas USA, whose shutdown led to the creation of LAFC and which shared Los Angeles (and their home stadium) with the LA Galaxy from 2005 to 2014 and often mock their fans as "plastics" who only became fans of both the club and the league recently.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maurer |first1=Pablo |last2=Stejskal |first2=Sam |date=October 27, 2020 |title=The short life and long death of Chivas USA |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2162943/2020/10/27/chivas-usa-history-mls/ |work=[[The Athletic]] |url-access=subscription |access-date=October 30, 2022}}</ref>

==Moniker==

"El Tráfico" (literally "The Traffic" in [[Spanish language|Spanish]]) was a name created by MLS fans and adopted by media outlets following polls by [[SB Nation]] blogs LAG Confidential<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.lagconfidential.com/2018/3/26/17164424/what-are-we-calling-the-la-galaxy-lafc-rivalry|title=What are we calling the LA Galaxy LAFC rivalry?|work=LAG Confidential|access-date=April 3, 2018}}</ref> and Angels on Parade.<ref name="Wiebe2018"/><ref name="LATimes-2018Mar"/><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.angelsonparade.com/2018/3/26/17165594/poll-what-should-we-call-the-lafc-la-galaxy-rivalry-battle-of-los-angeles-el-trafico-hollywood-derby|title=Poll: What should we call the LAFC-LA Galaxy rivalry?|work=Angels on Parade|access-date=April 3, 2018|archive-date=October 25, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221025134305/https://www.angelsonparade.com/2018/3/26/17165594/poll-what-should-we-call-the-lafc-la-galaxy-rivalry-battle-of-los-angeles-el-trafico-hollywood-derby|url-status=dead}}</ref> It refers to the notorious [[Transportation in Los Angeles|traffic congestion in Los Angeles]], among the worst in the United States and the world,<ref>{{cite news |date=February 6, 2018 |title=L.A.'s traffic congestion is world's worst for sixth straight year, study says |url=http://www.latimes.com/local/lanow/la-me-la-worst-traffic-20180206-story.html |work=Los Angeles Times |access-date=March 31, 2018}}</ref> while also serving as a pun on "[[El Clasico]]".<ref name="LATimes-2018Mar"/><ref>{{cite news |last=Davis |first=Matt |date=March 29, 2018 |title=Will Ferrell v Zlatan Ibrahimovic? Los Angeles FC prepare to face Galaxy on derby day |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/43238885 |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |access-date=March 31, 2018}}</ref> MLS has no plans to [[trademark]] the name.<ref>{{cite tweet |last=Lalas |first=Alexi |author-link=Alexi Lalas |user=AlexiLalas |date=March 28, 2018 |number=979044509563498496 |title=The first-ever @LAGalaxy vs. @LAFC game is Saturday 3 pm ET on @FOXTV. This LA derby is being called "El Tráfico." @MLS says the fans came up with the name and the League has no plans to trademark it. #ElTrafico #LAvLAFC |url=https://twitter.com/AlexiLalas/status/979044509563498496 |access-date=March 29, 2018}}</ref> The rivalry has also been called the "Los Angeles Derby",<ref>{{cite news |last=Lutz |first=Tom |date=March 31, 2018 |title=Zlatan Ibrahimovic's low-key MLS debut: a wondergoal then the winner for LA Galaxy |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/mar/31/zlatan-ibrahimovic-la-galaxy-debut-goal-mls-lafc-soccer |work=The Guardian |access-date=March 31, 2018}}</ref> a moniker that was also used for the SuperClasico.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Lalas |first=Greg |author-link=Greg Lalas |date=October 26, 2009 |title=L.A. derby finally means something |url=https://www.si.com/more-sports/2009/10/26/galaxy-chivas |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=March 31, 2018}}</ref> The name "El Tráfico" has faced opposition from executives within LAFC,<ref>{{cite news |last=Cardenas |first=Felipe |date=July 18, 2020 |title=The opposition to calling the LA Galaxy-LAFC rivalry 'El Tráfico' |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1935822/2020/07/18/the-opposition-to-calling-the-la-galaxy-lafc-rivalry-el-trafico/ |work=[[The Athletic]] |url-access=subscription |access-date=July 19, 2020}}</ref> coach Bob Bradley,<ref>{{cite news |last=Dwyer |first=Alex |date=March 4, 2019 |title=Bob Bradley dislikes "El Trafico" name for LA rivalry, offers "La Clasico" |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2019/03/04/bob-bradley-dislikes-el-trafico-name-la-rivalry-offers-la-clasico |work=MLSsoccer.com |access-date=July 19, 2020}}</ref> and the president of the 3252, LAFC's largest supporters group.<ref>{{cite news |last=Jones |first=J. Sam |date=March 30, 2020 |title=The inside story of what made first El Trafico matchup one of MLS's greatest ever games |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2020/03/30/inside-story-what-made-first-el-trafico-matchup-one-mlss-greatest-ever-games |publisher=Major League Soccer |work=MLSsoccer.com |access-date=July 19, 2020 |archive-date=March 4, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210304194541/https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2020/03/30/inside-story-what-made-first-el-trafico-matchup-one-mlss-greatest-ever-games |url-status=dead }}</ref>
